label: Botswana self-drive + great whites + Istanbul · Jan 15
title: Botswana self-drive and South Africa: Nxai Pan, the Central Kalahari, Moremi, Khwai and a Mossel Bay shark dive
summary: Self-drive 4x4 with a rooftop tent from Maun: Nxai Pan, the Boteti, 3 nights in the Central Kalahari for lions, cheetah and springbok herds, then Moremi and Khwai for leopards, wild dogs, hippos and elephants. A great white shark cage dive at Mossel Bay, then 3 nights in Istanbul on the way home. ~$5,400 pp.
overview:
- **What this is:** a camping self-drive through Botswana in the green season, which suits the Kalahari best: the pans and valleys turn green, springbok, gemsbok and zebra gather on them, and the **lions and cheetahs** follow. Then **Moremi and Khwai** on the edge of the Okavango for leopards, wild dogs, hippos and elephants, a **great white shark cage dive** in South Africa, and **3 nights in Istanbul** on the way home.
- **Dates:** LAX Sat Dec 26 → LAX Fri Jan 15. 17 nights on the ground: 2 Maun, **9 camping in parks**, 1 Cape Town, 2 Mossel Bay, 3 Istanbul, plus 3 on planes.
- **Route:** ✈ via Istanbul and Johannesburg to Maun 1n → **Nxai Pan 2n** → **Makgadikgadi (Khumaga) 1n** → **CKGR: Deception Valley 3n** → Maun 1n (refuel) → **Moremi (Xakanaxa) 1n** → **Khwai 2n** → ✈ Cape Town 1n → ✈ George → **Mossel Bay 2n** (shark dive + a spare morning) → ✈ Johannesburg → ✈ **Istanbul 3n** → home.
- **Cats:** Kalahari black-maned lions and cheetah on the open pans of Deception and Nxai, with brown hyena, caracal, bat-eared fox and honey badger possible. Leopard and wild dog are best in Khwai and Moremi.
- **Hippos and elephants:** hippo pools at Khwai and Xakanaxa and on the Boteti; elephant bulls at the Nxai Pan waterhole and herds along the Khwai.
- **Great whites:** Mossel Bay's Seal Island has been South Africa's most consistent great white site lately; Gansbaai's whites became sporadic after orcas moved in. Summer is the weaker season and sightings aren't guaranteed, so the plan has a spare morning for a second try.
- **Herps:** the rains bring out giant bullfrogs, plus puff adders, leopard tortoises, monitors and Nile crocodiles in the Okavango channels.
- **The catch:** you drive, cook and navigate yourselves in Botswana, on sand and black-clay mud after rain, with no fuel inside the parks. Self-drive isn't allowed after dark in the parks; carry the rental company's satellite communicator.
- **Istanbul at the end, not the start:** one Turkish ticket covers the long-haul, with the Stopover's 2 free hotel nights on the way home. You arrive in Botswana fresh, and the city is a slow wind-down after 9 nights of camping.
- **Budget: ~$5,400 pp** (≈ $10,800 for two), ~$285 more than ending the trip in South Africa: Istanbul's food, sights and one paid hotel night, less the Johannesburg hotel night that the Turkish routing makes unnecessary.

itinerary.title: Fly toward Johannesburg
itinerary.details: Turkish TK10 LAX 19:45 → Istanbul 19:00 next day (~13h). One Turkish ticket for the whole long-haul: out via Istanbul without stopping, home via Istanbul with 3 nights there.

itinerary.title: Connect in Istanbul
itinerary.details: Land Istanbul 19:00 and stay airside for Turkish's overnight flight to Johannesburg (older schedules show ~00:50 → 10:40; confirm the December times). Sleep on both flights if you can.

itinerary.title: Land in Johannesburg, fly on to Maun, collect the 4x4
itinerary.details: Land Johannesburg mid-morning, clear immigration and check in again for a midday Airlink flight to Maun (~1h45, several daily; leave 3h+ between them). Collect the vehicle in the afternoon: a Hilux or Land Cruiser with rooftop tent, fridge, kitchen box, two spare tyres, a long-range tank or jerry cans, and a satellite communicator. The handover takes ~2h; if it runs late, finish it first thing tomorrow. Shop for 5 days of food and 60+ litres of water. Botswana is UTC+2.

itinerary.title: East to Nxai Pan
itinerary.details: ~140 km of tar to the Nxai Pan turnoff, then ~35 km of deep sand to the gate (~3h total; deflate the tyres to ~1.6 bar). Afternoon at the main waterhole: elephant bulls, springbok, zebra arriving for the rains, lions often nearby. Camp at South Camp; lions and hyenas often walk past at night.

itinerary.title: Nxai Pan's green plains
itinerary.details: Zero transfer. Dawn on the pan for cheetah and lion on the zebra and springbok; the green season is when Nxai Pan is busiest with game. Midday rest. In the afternoon, Baines' Baobabs if the track is dry (it's on a salt pan and can be impassable after rain). Puff adders and bullfrogs on the tracks after a storm.

itinerary.title: To the Boteti River
itinerary.details: Back to the tar and south to Khumaga on the Boteti River (~2.5–3h). Hippos in the Boteti pools, elephants coming to drink, zebra and wildebeest on the west bank. New Year's Eve at Khumaga camp on the river.

itinerary.title: Into the Central Kalahari
itinerary.details: Via Rakops (last fuel: fill up) to the Matswere gate (~2h), then ~1h to Deception Valley. Afternoon drive along the valley: springbok, gemsbok, red hartebeest and wildebeest on the green grass, black-backed jackal, ground squirrels, and the resident lions. In the 1970s this was where Mark and Delia Owens studied brown hyenas and lions.

itinerary.title: Deception Valley and Sunday Pan
itinerary.details: Zero transfer. Dawn loop to Sunday Pan and Leopard Pan, the best area for lions and cheetah. Midday in camp under the shade sail. Afternoon back along Deception. Watch for bat-eared foxes, honey badgers, secretary birds, kori bustards.

itinerary.title: Kalahari lions
itinerary.details: Zero transfer. Another full day on the Deception–Sunday–Leopard Pan loops, timed around where the lions were the day before. After rain the clay pans are slippery: stay on the tracks.

itinerary.title: Out of the Kalahari to Maun
itinerary.details: Last dawn drive along Deception Valley, then north to Matswere gate, Rakops (fuel) and the tar to Maun (~4.5–5h). Shower, laundry, refuel, restock food and water.

itinerary.title: Into the Okavango side
itinerary.details: ~2h to Moremi's South Gate, then ~2h through mopane woodland and floodplain to Xakanaxa. Afternoon drive on the lagoons: hippos, crocodiles, red lechwe, elephants, and lion and leopard in the area. Tracks can be flooded after heavy rain; check at South Gate.

itinerary.title: Dawn drive, then Khwai
itinerary.details: Dawn drive around Xakanaxa and Dombo hippo pools, then ~1.5–2h east to North Gate and over the bridge into the Khwai community area. Afternoon along the Khwai River: elephants, hippos, leopard, wild dog den areas.

itinerary.title: Khwai: leopards and wild dogs
itinerary.details: Zero transfer. Dawn and afternoon along the Khwai River and Hippo Pools. Khwai is a community concession, so off-road driving and night drives are allowed, but only with a Khwai guide: book one for the evening (option).

itinerary.title: Back to Maun, fly to Cape Town
itinerary.details: Leave Khwai at first light (~3h via Shorobe), return the 4x4 by ~10:30, then Airlink Maun → Cape Town (13:50 → ~16:20, daily). Evening at the V&A Waterfront; hotel near the city or the airport.

itinerary.title: Fly to George, drive to Mossel Bay
itinerary.details: Morning flight Cape Town → George (~1h, FlySafair or Airlink). Pick up a small rental car; ~45 min west to Mossel Bay. Afternoon on the St Blaize cliff trail above the bay (dolphins, seabirds, sometimes whales offshore). Confirm tomorrow's boat time with the operator.

itinerary.title: Great white shark cage dive
itinerary.details: Morning boat from Mossel Bay harbour, ~10 min out to Seal Island (~4h trip). Breath-hold viewing from a surface cage with a wetsuit and mask; no scuba qualification needed. Great whites patrol the Cape fur seal colony; bronze whaler sharks are common too. Sightings aren't guaranteed, and summer has fewer whites than winter (May–August): ask the operator for its recent record and its policy on a repeat trip if no whites show. Afternoon free.

itinerary.location: Mossel Bay → George → Johannesburg → in flight
itinerary.title: Spare dive morning, fly to Istanbul
itinerary.details: Spare morning: if wind or swell cancelled yesterday's boat, this is the second chance. Otherwise a slow breakfast on the point. Drive to George airport, return the car, afternoon flight to Johannesburg (~2h), then Turkish's evening flight to Istanbul (older schedules show ~19:45 → ~06:00; confirm).

itinerary.title: Land in Istanbul, slow first day
itinerary.details: Land early morning. Airport metro (M11 → M2 → T1) to Sultanahmet, ~1.5h, or a taxi. Drop bags, nap, then an easy afternoon: the Blue Mosque and the Hippodrome, dinner nearby.

itinerary.title: Hagia Sophia, the Cistern, Topkapı
itinerary.details: Hagia Sophia and the Basilica Cistern at opening time, then Topkapı Palace. All within ten minutes' walk of each other. Zero travel.

itinerary.title: Grand Bazaar, Bosphorus ferry, Kadıköy
itinerary.details: Grand Bazaar and the Spice Bazaar in the morning, then a public ferry across the Bosphorus to Kadıköy on the Asian side for the food market and dinner. The ferry is the best view in the city and costs almost nothing.

itinerary.title: Fly home
itinerary.details: Free morning (Süleymaniye Mosque, or coffee by the Galata Bridge). Leave for the airport by ~11:00. TK9 14:30 → LAX 18:15 the same day (~13h45).

alternatives.name: Guided night drive in Khwai
alternatives.description: A Khwai community guide in your vehicle or theirs: leopards, genets, servals, owls, and snakes on the move. The only night driving on the trip.

alternatives.name: Boat trip from Mboma or Xakanaxa
alternatives.description: 2 hours on the Okavango channels: hippos up close, crocodiles, sitatunga, birds.

alternatives.description: 45–60 min over the Delta in a small plane; elephants, hippos and buffalo from the air.

alternatives.name: Guided mobile camping safari instead of self-drive
alternatives.description: Same route with a guide, cook and their vehicle. No driving, and night drives in Khwai, but well over budget.

alternatives.name: Keep Piper Pan instead of the shark dive
alternatives.description: 2 more Kalahari nights at Piper Pan instead of the South Africa stop: fly Maun → Johannesburg on Jan 10 and on to Istanbul.

alternatives.name: Gansbaai instead of Mossel Bay
alternatives.description: 2h from Cape Town, so no George flights. But great whites have become sporadic there since orcas moved in, and summer is the weakest season; most trips now see bronze whalers and sevengills instead.

alternatives.name: Skip Istanbul, home Jan 12
alternatives.description: Fly Johannesburg → home on the evening of Jan 11 via Doha, Dubai or Atlanta, and keep the Johannesburg hotel night on the way out.

practical:
## Entry
- **Botswana:** no visa for US citizens (up to 90 days). Pay the $30 Tourism Development Levy online beforehand. Passport valid 6+ months with 2 blank pages.
- **South Africa:** visa-free for US citizens (90 days); you enter twice (Dec 27 and Jan 8). Keep 2 blank pages for South Africa's stamps.
- **Türkiye:** visa-free for US citizens (90 days).
- **Yellow fever:** not required arriving from the US or Istanbul.

## Driving
- **Left-hand traffic.** Both drivers need a US licence; an International Driving Permit is advisable.
- Deflate to ~1.6 bar in sand; re-inflate on the tar. Never drive the parks after dark (it's illegal in the national parks, and there are elephants and cattle on the tar at night).
- **Black-clay mud** on the CKGR pans and around Nxai after rain: stay on the tracks, don't cross a wet pan, and turn back rather than get stuck alone.
- Carry 20+ litres of water each beyond drinking needs, and the satellite communicator. Tell the rental firm your route.
- No fuel in any park. Last fuel before the CKGR is Rakops.

## Camping
- Unfenced sites: lions, hyenas and elephants walk through. Sleep in the rooftop tent, zip up, never walk away from the car after dark, and keep food in the vehicle.
- Bring firewood from Maun; collecting it in the parks isn't allowed.

## Money
- Botswana pula. Cards work in Maun; carry cash (pula) for park gates, firewood and tips.

## Season
- December–March: hot days (~32–38 °C), warm nights, afternoon thunderstorms. The Kalahari is at its greenest and best for game; Moremi's game is more spread out than in the dry season, but there are far fewer vehicles.

## Health and safety
- Check travel.state.gov for Botswana before booking.
- Remote: the nearest hospital is in Maun. Evacuation cover is essential.

## Shark dive
- Breath-hold viewing from a surface cage, so there's no diving-then-flying problem the next day.
- Seasickness: take a tablet before the boat if you're prone; the Atlantic swell off Mossel Bay can be lumpy.
- Trips are weather-dependent and get cancelled in strong wind; Jan 11 morning is the backup.

## Istanbul in January
- Cold and often wet (~4–9 °C): pack a warm layer and a rain jacket, which you'll want on Kalahari dawn drives anyway.

scores.scale: 1–5, for late December and early January. Crowds: 1 = you rarely see another vehicle, 5 = queues of vehicles at sightings (lower is better). Wildlife numbers: how many animals you see. Wildlife diversity: how many different kinds. These are judgments from how each place works in this season, not counts.

overall.note: The emptiest of the four in Botswana, then a busier, very different finish at sea. You'll see a smaller share of the cats in Botswana, because nobody is tracking them for you.

sites.name: Nxai Pan
sites.note: A handful of vehicles at the main waterhole at most. In the rains zebra, springbok and wildebeest pour onto the grassland, and lions and cheetah follow; elephant bulls at the waterhole.

sites.name: Makgadikgadi (Khumaga)
sites.note: Very quiet. Hippos and elephants on the Boteti; most zebra move out onto the pans in the rains, so fewer herds than in the dry season.

sites.name: Central Kalahari: Deception Valley
sites.note: Often no other vehicle at your pan. Thousands of springbok and gemsbok on the green valleys, with giraffe, lions, cheetah and bat-eared foxes. Desert species only: no hippos, few elephants.

sites.name: Moremi (Xakanaxa)
sites.note: Low season, but the Delta's best-known self-drive camp. Wet-season game is spread out, but the habitat mix is the richest on the trip: hippos, crocodiles, lechwe, elephants, lion, leopard, wild dog.

sites.name: Khwai
sites.note: South African school holidays run into mid-January, and Khwai is a favourite of self-drivers and lodge vehicles, which bunch up at leopard and wild dog sightings. Excellent for elephants, hippos and cats.

sites.name: Mossel Bay (shark dive)
sites.note: A few operators' boats share Seal Island, but you're in the water with the sharks. Thousands of Cape fur seals; great whites possible (fewer in summer), bronze whalers likely, dolphins on the boat ride.

sites.name: Istanbul
sites.note: Mid-January is after the New Year rush: busy at the big sights, but far calmer than the holiday weeks.

pros: Emptiest by far: whole pans to yourselves in the Kalahari.
The Kalahari's green season (big springbok and gemsbok herds, lions and cheetah on open ground) happens only now.
Three very different parts: desert pans, the Okavango's rivers, and great whites at sea.
Still the cheapest of the four (~$5,400), and you set the pace in Botswana.
cons: You drive, navigate, camp and cook; long sand and mud days, and the risk of getting stuck alone.
No guide: fewer cat sightings (leopards especially), and no night drives except a guided one in Khwai.
Great whites aren't guaranteed in January, and the South Africa leg adds three flights.
Basic or no facilities at the Kalahari and Khwai sites; hot (32–38 °C) with thunderstorms.
